sourceDocuments.note: Passes the input fields as individual variables and sends phoneIsVerified/emailIsVerified.
Same individual-variable shape and the same client-supplied verification flags.

securityDecisions: Client verification flags are never trusted or written: the lane rule derives verification from a consumed server challenge only. The response reports persisted state (IdentityUser.emailVerified); phoneIsVerified is false because no server-side phone proof can exist until the challenge store lands.
The root always targets the authenticated principal: the input type has no id or email selector, so there is no ownership argument to forge.

A phone already owned by another account returns CONFLICT and leaves the caller's row untouched; absent or null phone leaves the stored number unchanged; malformed name or number is BAD_USER_INPUT before any write.

commands.command: pnpm --filter @fairbite/api exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts test/unit/identity/updateUser.spec.ts
commands.detail: 2 tests: the profile input and context are forwarded; a missing input object degrades to {} instead of undefined.

6 tests: exact app and web documents; name trim and phone normalization persisted; client flags ignored in both directions (unverified stays false, server-verified stays true); taken phone is CONFLICT with no change; malformed input changes nothing; anonymous refused and another principal untouched.

evidenceStatus.reason: The apps list is app and web, so the evidence checker requires web (W16) and device (W19) evidence. The record stays NOT_VERIFIED.

knownLimits: Because no challenge store exists yet, phoneIsVerified can never become true through this root; the pinned phone-verification screen will therefore read an honest unverified state until the OTP/challenge slice lands. That is the truthful outcome, not a fabricated success.
The OTP documents also pass a client-supplied otp argument to the send mutations; that needs its own design round before sendOtpToEmail/sendOtpToPhoneNumber/verifyOtp are implemented.
